claims.text: An active-learning MLIP integrated with enhanced thermodynamic integration can capture solid–liquid free-energy differences at fusion.
The proposed method can retain vibrational, anharmonic, and configurational entropy contributions.
The proposed method will have fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by roughly an order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD.
Active learning can select a representative subset of ab initio configurations for training an interatomic potential.
The trained MLIP will be used in thermodynamic-integration molecular dynamics for both solid and fluid phases.
The method is primarily valid for elemental and binary refractory systems near melting.
Vibrational and anharmonic effects are non-negligible at high temperatures near fusion.
Initial tests should span approximately 0.8–1.2 times the expected melting temperature.
Accurate representation of interatomic interactions and anharmonicity by the MLIP will reproduce phase-dependent entropy contributions.
Updating the MLIP through active learning will preserve fine vibrational and configurational entropy details in free-energy calculations.
MLIP-driven molecular dynamics will run at a fraction of the cost of explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Free-energy and melting-point predictions will be within approximately 5% of explicit ab initio values.
The proposed workflow will be 10–20 times faster than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will be more computationally efficient than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
Explicit ab initio workflows are computationally demanding for compositionally complex refractory alloys.
Extension of the method to multicomponent high-entropy alloys is uncertain pending validation.
Extreme anharmonicity and increasing compositional complexity may reduce MLIP fidelity or active-learning robustness.
